predecessors.name: Republic of Florence
predecessors.text: the Medici grand duchy at Gian Gastone's death on 9 July 1737: Florence, Pisa, Livorno, Arezzo, Siena and the Maremma

successors.name: United Provinces of Central Italy
successors.text: the Grand Duchy as it stood in 1859, joined to Modena and Parma on 8 December 1859

ledger.x: 9 July 1737: the Medici line ends and Tuscany passes to the House of Lorraine.
21 March 1801: the Grand Duchy is abolished and replaced by the Kingdom of Etruria.
30 May 1814: the Grand Duchy is re-established.
1815: the State of the Presidi passes to Tuscany.
1847: Tuscany gives up its Lunigiana domains.
17 December 1847: the Duchy of Lucca reverts to Tuscany.
February 1849: the Grand Duke flees and republicans take Tuscany.
April 1849: the grand-ducal government is restored.
16 August 1859: the House of Habsburg-Lorraine is deposed.
8 December 1859: Tuscany joins Modena and Parma in the United Provinces of Central Italy.

wars.name: Napoleonic wars in Tuscany (1799-1814)
wars.outcome: A Provisional Government was created by the French army in spring 1799; the Grand Duchy was dissolved by the Treaty of Aranjuez (21 March 1801) into the Kingdom of Etruria, which the Treaty of Fontainebleau (27 October 1807) annexed to France on 30 May 1808…

wars.name: Tuscan revolution of 1848-1849
wars.outcome: Leopold II sanctioned a liberal constitution in 1848, left Tuscany to republicans in February 1849 and came back with Austrian help.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence (Tuscany 1859)
wars.outcome: Leopold II left Florence on 27 April 1859, abdicated on 21 July, was deposed on 16 August; Tuscany joined the United Provinces of Central Italy on 8 December 1859 and was annexed to Sardinia on 22 March 1860.

certainty.note: The long-settled Medici-Lorraine frontiers; the Lunigiana and Garfagnana enclaves and exclaves are not delineated on the pages opened.
No grand duchy: Kingdom of Etruria, then France; kept so the certainty covers the dossier's years.
Frontiers fixed by the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815) and the 1844 Treaty of Florence (1847); the Tuscan frontier with Lucca disappears on 17 December 1847.
